prop:toffoli-lp-stability:
Proposition LP-dual stability of the q-Toffoli braid and the golden-ratio threshold. Let T_q \in H_3(q) be the q-Toffoli element, realized as the 3-strand braid word with traced volume matrix M(q). Let G = (\mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j))_{i,j} be the Gram matrix of the normal-form basis. Express the q-Toffoli in normal-form coordinates as T_q = \sum_{i=1}^{6} t_i(q) \, b_i. Then:

  1. (Stability region.) With Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the amplitudes the Toffoli construction produces are
  P_{6,6} = \frac{(q^4+1)(q^4+q^2+2)}{4q(q^2+1)^2},
  \qquad
  P_{7,7} = \frac{q^3(q^4+1)}{(q^2+1)^2},
  P_{7,6} = -\frac{(q-1)(q+1)(q^6+q^4+2q^2+1)}{2q(q^2+1)^2},
  \qquad
  P_{6,7} = \frac{(q-1)(q+1)(2q^6+q^4+q^2+1)}{2q(q^2+1)^2}.

The two diagonal amplitudes are strictly positive on q > 0; each off-diagonal amplitude has exactly one zero there, at q = 1, since its sextic factor is positive for every real q. Thus the Toffoli amplitude family has one operator zero on (0,\infty), at q = 1, and P_{7,6} < 0 for every q > 1 — including the aether value.

  1. (The operator threshold.) The derived family has a single threshold on (0,\infty): See Table 1. At q = 1 both off-diagonal amplitudes vanish through their common factor (q-1): the classical reversible Toffoli has trivial off-diagonal amplitude. Neither diagonal amplitude vanishes anywhere on q > 0, and neither off-diagonal sextic factor has a positive real root, so q = 1 is the sole positive threshold.

  2. (Dual shadow prices.) For q > 1, the LP dual admits bounded shadow prices y_i^*(q) satisfying:

  |y_i^*(q)| \leq \kappa(\mathrm{G}(q)) \cdot \|t(q)\|,

where \kappa(\mathrm{G}(q)) = \lambda_{\max}(G)/|\lambda_{\min}(G)|. Open boundary (Gram radical). Because y_{(1^3)} = 0 at z = q^3/(q^2+1), the Markov–Gram form on H_3(q) is singular, so \lambda_{\max}/|\lambda_{\min}| in the ordinary sense is infinite on the full six-dimensional normal-form span; formulating a finite shadow-price bound requires passing to the quotient by the radical, as in Term 4 of the six-term mass identity.

  1. (Physical-aether stability — the positivity reduction does not hold as stated.) At q_0 \approx 1.110 (with z = q^3/(q^2+1)):
  P_{7,7}(q_0) \,\approx\, 0.6912,
  \qquad
  P_{7,6}(q_0) \,\approx\, -0.1438.

The diagonal is strictly positive; the target-flip amplitude is negative, and is negative throughout q > 1.

The stability argument recorded in the proof block runs through the positivity of both amplitudes, so it does not close on the derived family. What that costs is bounded by which step it enters: the proof reduces feasibility of G\vec t(q) \geq 0 to the positivity of P_{7,7}(q)\,W_{\mathrm{std}}(q) "with the appropriate sign from P_{7,6}(q)", and that qualifying clause is asserted without derivation — nothing in the corpus says what the sign is or why. The first factor survives: P_{7,7}(q_0)\,W_{\mathrm{std}}(q_0) \approx 0.4624 > 0.

The stated condition has now been measured directly, and it holds. Rather than settle the reduction, one can construct T_q and evaluate G\vec t(q_0) \geq 0 itself. The element is implicit in the crossing coefficients — C_{ij} = c_j\sigma_i + d_j is an algebra element, and the chain recursion is (a\sigma+b)(c\sigma+d) reduced by \sigma^2 = \hbar_\times\sigma + 1 — so for the all-proton ordering

  T_q \;=\; \sigma_1 \;+\; \hbar_\times\,\sigma_0\sigma_1,
  \qquad \hbar_\times = q - q^{-1}.

Against the H_3(q) Markov–Gram matrix, every component of G\vec t(q_0) is strictly positive, for all eight strand-type orderings. So the aether satisfies the LP condition this proposition states.

Two qualifications, both of which bound what that is worth. First, the Gram is entrywise non-negative, and \vec t is too for the all-proton ordering, so for that ordering positivity is forced by shape with no cancellation possible — 2 of the 8 orderings are trivial in this sense and 6 are not. Second, and more consequential: \vec t acquires a negative component exactly when \hbar_\times < 0, i.e. on 0 < q < 1 — the opposite side of q = 1 from where P_{7,6} is negative. The amplitude sign and the cone condition disagree about which regime is the admissible one, so the reduction above does not merely mix index spaces.

That sign inversion is now proved to be an identity, and it excludes the reduction as written. Since \hbar_\times = (q-1)(q+1)/q, the flip amplitude factors as

  P_{7,6}(q) \;=\; -\,\hbar_\times\,\cdot\,\frac{S(q)}{2(q^2+1)^2},
  \qquad S(q) = q^6+q^4+2q^2+1,

and S has no real root while (q^2+1)^2 > 0, so the cofactor is strictly positive on all of \mathbb{R}. The flip amplitude is therefore -\hbar_\times times something positive, while the cone coordinate is +\hbar_\times — giving P_{7,6}(q)\,\hbar_\times(q) \leq 0 for every q > 0. This is proved, with an independent symbolic cross-check.

This is a scope-(b) exclusion, and the invariant is the factorisation above: no reduction in which the cone condition inherits the flip amplitude's sign can hold at any q > 0, because the two carry exactly opposite signs of the same factor. It does not exclude a reduction carrying a negative proportionality — one in which the cone condition follows -P_{7,6} — and that is the natural remaining candidate.

No claim of LP-instability is made, and none is available: the condition as stated is satisfied. The downstream statement that \{q\text{-Toffoli}, H\} generates universal reversible computation on the Reeb bundles inherits that opening.

Every sign and zero claim above is proved. Nothing in this arc rests on evaluation at a single anchor:

claim
P_{7,7} > 0 on q > 0, no positive root
P_{6,6} > 0 on q > 0
P_{7,6}'s only positive zero is q = 1
P_{7,6} < 0 on q > 1, the aether side
P_{7,6} > 0 on 0 < q < 1
P_{6,7} + P_{7,6} = q(q-1)^2(q+1)^2/2(q^2+1)
the flip channel is not antisymmetric
W_{\mathrm{std}} > 0 and P_{7,7}W_{\mathrm{std}} > 0
\mathrm{sign}\,P_{7,6} = -\mathrm{sign}\,\hbar_\times

The antisymmetry defect is exact and vanishes only at q = 1, so "reversing the crossing negates it" fails everywhere except the classical limit.

The reduction is refuted by a zero-set argument. The proof reduces the cone condition to P_{7,7}W_{\mathrm{std}} "with the appropriate sign from" P_{7,6}. A product vanishes exactly where a factor does, so such a reduction forces the cone condition's zero set into the union of the factors'. With the symbolic Gram — validated against the numerical Gram matrix at five values of q — the cone condition is a single constraint, the one indexed by the longest word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0:

  (G\vec t)_5 \;=\; \frac{q^{10}+q^{6}-q^{4}+q^{2}-1}{(q^2+1)^2}
quantity zeros on q > 0
the cone constraint (G\vec t)_5 one, at q_c \approx 0.8944802929
P_{7,7}W_{\mathrm{std}} = (q^7+q^3)/(q^4+4q^2+1) none — strictly positive
P_{7,6} one, at q = 1

Since q_c \neq 1, the cone's zero is accounted for by neither factor, so no reduction of the stated form holds. The numerator is irreducible over \mathbb{Q} and has exactly one positive real root, matching the bisected threshold to 1.14\times10^{-46}. Proved without the intermediate value theorem and without q_c's value: across [1/2, 9/10] the cone constraint changes sign while both claimed factors stay strictly positive at each endpoint.

Why the reduction had to fail: the relation exists, but at degree 2. The eight amplitudes generate the whole field \mathbb{Q}(q) — four of them reconstruct q itself, via M_{33}/M_{44} = q^4 and P_{7,7}/M_{00} = q^6 — so asking whether the cone condition is some rational expression in them has no content. Restricting the form does. Over the common denominator q^6(q^2+1)^4 the ambient space of numerators is 21-dimensional, and the degree-2 span of the amplitudes has rank 15: a proper subspace of codimension 6, which a generic rational function does not meet. The cone constraint is in it, and four amplitudes already suffice:

\[
\begin{aligned}
  (G\vec t)_5 \;={}& -\tfrac{4}{9}
  \;+\; \tfrac{5}{36}M_{00}^2 \;-\; \tfrac{20}{3}M_{00}M_{33} \;-\; \tfrac{10}{9}M_{00}M_{44} \;+\; \tfrac{5}{18}M_{00}P_{7,7} \\
  &\;-\; \tfrac{28}{9}M_{33}^2 \;+\; \tfrac{20}{3}M_{33}M_{44} \;+\; \tfrac{38}{9}M_{33}P_{7,7} \;+\; \tfrac{20}{9}M_{44}^2 \;+\; \tfrac{5}{36}P_{7,7}^2
\end{aligned}
\]

This identity is proved, together with the transfer of sign from the numerator to the constraint. Only + and \times appear: no division by an amplitude, hence no reconstruction of q. The cross terms are load-bearing — the span of the amplitudes and their squares alone has rank 14 and does not contain the constraint.

This sharpens the refutation rather than softening it. A monomial vanishes exactly where a factor does; a degree-2 polynomial can vanish where none of its terms does, and that is precisely the mechanism producing the root at q_c. So the published reduction was the right kind of relation in the wrong class: it needed cancellation between products, which a single product cannot supply. Whether any member of the (one-parameter) solution family has a Hecke-theoretic reading is open.

The natural coordinates are the Markov and Hecke parameters, and there the expression is forced. The rational coefficients above are a fact about the amplitude basis, not about the constraint. Writing z = q^3/(q^2+1) for the Markov parameter and \hbar_\times = q - 1/q for the Hecke deformation of \sigma^2 = \hbar_\times\sigma + 1,

  (G\vec t)_5 \;=\; z^2 \;+\; 2\hbar_\times z \;+\; 3\hbar_\times^2 z^2 \;+\; \hbar_\times^3 z \;+\; \hbar_\times^4 z^2 ,

with integer coefficients (1,2,3,1,1) and no denominators. Degree 6 is minimal — no polynomial in (z,\hbar_\times) of total degree \leq 5 equals it — and minimal degree is a genuine invariant of the class. The polynomial identity is proved.

The coefficient string, however, is not an invariant. The two parameters are algebraically dependent, satisfying the irreducible degree-4 relation

  \hbar_\times^3 z - \hbar_\times^2 z^2 + 4\hbar_\times z - 4z^2 + 1 \;=\; 0 ,

so \mathbb{Q}[z,\hbar_\times] is not a polynomial ring but the coordinate ring of an affine rational curve, and a polynomial representative is unique only modulo that relation. The degree-6 representatives form a six-parameter family: -1 + 4z^2 - 3\hbar_\times z + 4z^4 + \hbar_\times^2 z^4 is an equally integral one, differing from the first by (\hbar_\times z + z^2 + 1) times the relation. A reproducible choice is the grevlex normal form \hbar_\times^5 z + 4\hbar_\times^3 z + \hbar_\times^2 - 2\hbar_\times z + 5z^2 - 1, but even that depends on the term order. The relation is a fact about H_n(q) and its Markov trace, not about the q-Toffoli.

This is forced, not fitted. Every Markov trace of a Hecke word lies in \mathbb{Z}[z,\hbar_\times] — the Markov property \mathrm{tr}(x\sigma_{\mathrm{last}}) = z\,\mathrm{tr}(x) removes the highest generator and the quadratic relation reduces the rest — and in particular \hbar_\times z^2 + z = \mathrm{tr}(\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0). Since the q-Toffoli's normal-form coordinates are \vec t = (0,0,1,\hbar_\times,0,0), that is T_q = \sigma_1 + \hbar_\times\sigma_0\sigma_1, the constraint (G\vec t)_5 = \mathrm{tr}(W\sigma_1) + \hbar_\times\mathrm{tr}(W\sigma_0\sigma_1) lies in \mathbb{Z}[z,\hbar_\times] before any computation is done.

Both parameters are needed: the constraint's minimal polynomial over \mathbb{Q}(z) has degree 3 and over \mathbb{Q}(\hbar_\times) degree 2, so it is a function of neither alone. Since those degrees are coprime, \mathbb{Q}(z,\hbar_\times) = \mathbb{Q}(q) and the content is the subring statement, not a field one. Separately, the numerator is neither reciprocal nor anti-reciprocal, so it is the Alexander polynomial of no knot — a scope-(b) exclusion resting on the reciprocity invariant.

Proof Proof of toffoli lp stability. The Gram matrix G over H_3(q) has a characteristic polynomial whose eigenvalue crossings are controlled by the discriminant of the Hecke relation (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0. The smallest eigenvalue \lambda_{\min}(\mathrm{G}(q)) is continuous in q. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the bilinear pairing \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j) carries one negative eigenvalue, \lambda_{\min}(q_0) = -0.75270211 (with a one-dimensional radical from y_{(1^3)} = 0), whereas on the star pairing \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j^*) the form is positive semidefinite with signature (5,0,1). Any sign claim here must name which pairing it means.

Write T_q in the NF basis. The target-flip amplitude P_{7,6}(q) determines the off-diagonal mass component. The diagonal P_{7,7}(q) determines the Wedderburn weight of the standard channel (Toffoli transfer matrix). Positivity of G\vec{t}(q) therefore reduces to the positivity of the product P_{7,7}(q) \cdot W_{\mathrm{std}}(q) with the appropriate sign from the off-diagonal amplitude.

Open step — the second half of the reduction is underived. The derived off-diagonal amplitude is

  P_{7,6}(q) \;=\; -\frac{(q-1)(q+1)(q^6+q^4+2q^2+1)}{2q(q^2+1)^2}

(Toffoli transfer matrix). The reduction above is asserted in a single clause and the part that carries the weight — "with the appropriate sign from" the off-diagonal amplitude — is not derived: nothing states what that sign must be, or why. The first factor satisfies P_{7,7}(q)\,W_{\mathrm{std}}(q) > 0 for all q > 0; the second is open.

Solving P_{7,7}(q) = 0 on (0,\infty): the numerator is q^3(q^4+1), whose only real zero is q = 0, so the derived diagonal has no positive zero.

Solving P_{7,6}(q) = 0 on (0,\infty): the factor (q-1) gives q = 1; the factor (q+1) has no positive root; and q^6 + q^4 + 2q^2 + 1 > 0 for every real q. So q = 1 is the only positive zero.

For q > 1: P_{7,7}(q) > 0 but P_{7,6}(q) < 0, since the sextic factor is positive and the sign is carried by -(q-1)(q+1). The Wedderburn weights W_{\mathrm{sym}} = W_{\mathrm{alt}} = q^2/(q^4 + 4q^2 + 1) and W_{\mathrm{std}} = (q^2+1)^2/(q^4 + 4q^2 + 1) are strictly positive. So the sign pattern on the physical regime is mixed, not uniformly positive: the amplitudes of the derived family are not all of the same sign. Whether linear reduction preserves feasibility under a mixed pattern is the open step above; item 4 of the proposition evaluates G\vec t(q_0) directly instead.

For 0 < q < 1: P_{7,6}(q) > 0. The sign reversal of the off-diagonal amplitude occurs at q = 1 and nowhere else.

The boundedness of shadow prices is not a consequence of LP duality (LP-dual stability states only feasibility and strong duality). The bound used here is the one recorded in the confinement reading: the dual norm |y^*| bounded by the primal norm times the Gram condition number \kappa(\mathrm{G}(q)) = \lambda_{\max}(G)/|\lambda_{\min}(G)|. Open step (Gram singularity). At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the Markov–Gram form is singular (y_{(1^3)} = 0), so the ratio \lambda_{\max}/|\lambda_{\min}| is not a finite condition number on the full six-dimensional normal-form span. Moreover, at q_0, P_{7,7}(q_0) \approx 0.6912 > 0 whereas P_{7,6}(q_0) \approx -0.1438 < 0. Closing the shadow-price bound requires passing to the quotient by the radical, and closing the amplitude step requires deriving the off-diagonal sign relation. \square

Physical consequence. The aether parameter q_0 \approx 1.110 sits on the q > 1 side of the single threshold q = 1, where the diagonal amplitudes are positive and P_{7,6}(q_0) is negative.

prop:q-game-of-life:
Proposition The quantum Game of Life (q-GoL) as a Toffoli-defined aether automaton. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with aether parameter q and Planck time t_P(q) = 1/\hbar_q. Let \mathcal{L} \subset M be a discrete sublattice of brane points \{p_i\}. Each site carries a qubit |\psi_i\rangle \in \mathcal{S}_{p_i}. The q-Game of Life (q-GoL) is the discrete-time invertible cellular automaton

  \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}}
    \colon  \mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{L}}
    \to  \mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{L}},
  \qquad
  |\Psi(t{+}1)\rangle
   = 
  \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}}
  |\Psi(t)\rangle.

The operator \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}} is constructed entirely from q-deformed Toffoli gates acting on Reeb bundle fibres of neighbour sites. The construction requires five properties:

  1. Building block. The transition operator is the q-AND gate:
  \mathrm{Toff}_q
  \colon  |c_1, c_2, t\rangle
  \longmapsto
  |c_1, c_2,  t \oplus_q (c_1 \wedge_q c_2)\rangle.

The symbol \wedge_q denotes the Hecke-algebra q-AND amplitude P_{7,6}(q), given under Well-definedness condition below. Each \mathrm{Toff}_q executes in three Planck steps.

No control-independent factor \Phi(q) lies in the image of the three-strand Toffoli construction (Toffoli transfer matrix); \wedge_q is evaluated directly via P_{7,6}(q).

  1. Superposition. Cell states admit superpositions |\psi_i\rangle = \alpha_i|0\rangle + \beta_i|1\rangle via Hadamard rotations H \in \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{S}_{p_i}). The set \{\mathrm{Toff}_q, H\} is universal for reversible computation, in the sense of Bennett, for every q > 0: reversible universality needs the gate to be invertible with a firing target-flip channel, both of which item 4 and the non-vanishing of P_{7,6} on q \neq 1 supply.

Scope of universality. The standard Toffoli-plus-Hadamard quantum universality theorem applies to unitary gates, whereas \mathrm{Toff}_q is provably not unitary for q \neq 1. Whether a non-unitary invertible gate set can be universal in a quantum sense is unsettled, so item 2 states reversible universality only.

  1. Conway's rules as Toffoli circuits. Survival (k = 2, 3) and birth (k = 3) at site i with neighbourhood N(i) are enacted by the composite operator
  \mathcal{U}_i^{\mathrm{rule}}
   = 
  \prod_{\{j_1, j_2\} \subset N(i)}
  \mathrm{Toff}_q
  \!\left(
    |\psi_{j_1}\rangle,  |\psi_{j_2}\rangle;  |\psi_i\rangle
  \right).

Ancilla qubits encode the neighbour sum. A ripple-carry adder of O(|N(i)|) Toffoli gates computes the binary count k.

  1. Reversibility. Each \mathrm{Toff}_q is invertible, with
  \sigma_i^{-1}
   = 
  \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1})\cdot \mathbb{1},

so \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}} is invertible and the automaton is reversible. It is not unitary away from the classical limit: the eigenvalues of \sigma_i are q and -q^{-1}, of modulus \neq 1 for q \neq 1, so no inner product makes \mathrm{Toff}_q unitary, and the Markov trace form has a nontrivial radical at z = q^3/(q^2+1). Reversibility in the sense a reversible cellular automaton requires — invertibility of the tick — therefore holds for every q > 0, being a property of the quadratic relation alone and independent of the amplitude signs discussed below; unitarity holds only at q = 1.

  1. Information bandwidth budget. One generation advances in 3 |\mathcal{L}| Planck steps. The aether bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q) = q \eta_q / (q - 1)^2 bounds the generation rate:
  \text{gens / sec}
   \leq 
  \frac{\mathfrak{B}(q)}{3  |\mathcal{L}|}
   = 
  \frac{q \eta_q}{3  (q - 1)^2  |\mathcal{L}|}.

Well-definedness condition. The evolution is well-defined only when the Toffoli diagonal P_{7,7}(q) is positive and the q-AND amplitude P_{7,6}(q) is non-zero. With Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the two amplitudes are

  P_{7,7}(q) \,=\, \frac{q^{3}\bigl(q^{4}+1\bigr)}{\bigl(q^{2}+1\bigr)^{2}},
  \qquad
  P_{7,6}(q) \,=\, -\,\frac{(q-1)(q+1)\bigl(q^{6}+q^{4}+2q^{2}+1\bigr)}{2q\bigl(q^{2}+1\bigr)^{2}}.

For q > 0 the first is strictly positive, having no positive root. The second vanishes exactly at q = 1: the factor (q+1) is positive there, and the sextic q^{6}+q^{4}+2q^{2}+1 has no positive real root, so the whole zero set on q > 0 is carried by (q-1). The condition therefore holds on q \neq 1, which contains the aether value q_0 \approx 1.110.

Non-vanishing, not positivity. The criterion is that the q-AND does not degenerate, not that it carry a particular sign. This is the same condition the universality argument of Toffoli q-AND uses — it turns on P_{7,6}(q) \neq 0 — and it is what invertibility of the tick requires. At q = 1 the q-AND vanishes and the braiding ceases to act: that is the classical limit, where the q-Toffoli degenerates to the ordinary Toffoli, and it is the one point the condition excludes.

Strict positivity would be a different and stronger requirement: at z = q^3/(q^2+1) it holds only on 0 < q < 1, since P_{7,6}(q_0) \approx -0.1438, and would place the aether outside the well-defined regime. It is not the criterion in force here.

Direct LP feasibility vs. amplitude sign. Constructing the q-Toffoli as an element of H_3(q) — T_q = \sigma_1 + \hbar_\times\,\sigma_0\sigma_1 for the all-proton ordering — and evaluating the LP condition G\vec t(q_0) \geq 0 directly against the H_3(q) Markov–Gram matrix gives strictly positive components for all eight strand-type orderings (Toffoli LP-stability). Thus the aether satisfies LP feasibility as well as non-vanishing. Two structural properties qualify this: first, the Gram matrix is entrywise non-negative and \vec t is entrywise non-negative for the all-proton ordering, so positivity is forced by shape for 2 of the 8 orderings and nontrivial for the remaining 6; second, \vec t turns negative on 0 < q < 1, the opposite side of q = 1 from where P_{7,6}(q) < 0, so the amplitude sign and the LP cone condition select opposite regimes.

Proof Proof of q game of life. The operator \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}} is built from q-Toffoli generators. By Toffoli transfer matrix, these act as elements of H_3(q) \otimes \cdots \otimes H_3(q) on the tensor product of Reeb bundles \bigotimes_i \mathcal{S}_{p_i}. Each generator is invertible in H_n(q), and it is invertibility — not unitarity — that this argument establishes. For real q > 0 with q \neq 1, the eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} of \sigma_i have modulus \neq 1, so \sigma_i is not unitary with respect to any positive-definite inner product (by contrast, Squier's invariant bar-Hermitian form over \mathbb{Z}[s, s^{-1}] with s^2 = t is indefinite away from the unit circle [squier1984, Theorem, p. 199; \S 3, eq. (6), p. 201]); and the Markov trace form is not available as a Hilbert inner product on H_n(q), having a nontrivial radical at z = q^3/(q^2+1) for n \ge 3. Reversibility therefore rests on invertibility alone: the quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 gives the explicit inverse

  \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1})\cdot 1 ,

so every \sigma_i is a unit and the composite is invertible. The generators are not involutions at generic q: \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i holds precisely when q = q^{-1}, i.e. in the classical limit q \to 1, which is where the q-Toffoli reduces to the ordinary Toffoli gate.

Any reversible computation is simulated by Toffoli gates [bennett1973, toffoli1980, fredkin1982]. That Toffoli together with Hadamard is universal for quantum computation is the theorem of Shi and of Aharonov [shi2002, aharonov2003], stated for the standard Toffoli gate; its extension to \mathrm{Toff}_q at q \neq 1 is not established here.

The bandwidth bound follows by counting. Each \mathrm{Toff}_q in the 3-strand Hecke algebra requires three elementary crossings, taking three Planck steps. One generation applies one Toffoli gate per neighbour triple. This yields the stated bound.

The well-definedness condition requires P_{7,7}(q) > 0 and P_{7,6}(q) \neq 0. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the diagonal is P_{7,7}(q) = q^{3}(q^{4}+1)/(q^{2}+1)^{2}; numerator and denominator are strictly positive for every q > 0, so the first clause holds throughout and places no constraint. The q-AND is P_{7,6}(q) = -(q-1)(q+1)(q^{6}+q^{4}+2q^{2}+1)/\bigl(2q(q^{2}+1)^{2}\bigr); for q > 0 the factor (q+1) is positive and the sextic has no positive real root, so the zero set is exactly \{q = 1\} and the second clause holds on q \neq 1. The condition therefore holds on q \neq 1, which contains the aether. \square

Note that the criterion used here is non-vanishing, not positivity: invertibility of the tick and the universality argument of Toffoli q-AND require only P_{7,6}(q) \neq 0. Strict positivity would restrict to 0 < q < 1 and exclude the aether.
rem:q-game-of-life-interpretation:
Remark Deterministic cellular-automaton models of Peña et al. and 't Hooft. Peña et al. construct a reversible quantum Game of Life using Toffoli-based adder circuits. Their Toffoli gate is the classical limit q \to 1 of the q-Toffoli, and their construction is recovered in that limit; away from it the two are not comparable, since the q-deformed generator is invertible but not unitary. Their unitary tick maps to 3 Planck steps. One identifies the q-deformed amplitude P_{7,6}(q) as the physical AND amplitude. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) it has a single zero on q > 0, at q = 1, and the diagonal P_{7,7}(q) has none. sec:skein-trace-bandwidth-intro: Evaluating a braid closure through the skein resolution tree expands c crossings into 3^c resolution leaves, whereas evaluating the trace of a product of c matrices of fixed dimension d takes at most d^3 c ring multiplications. def:computational-horizon:
Definition Computational horizon. Let L = \hat{\beta} be the braid closure of a computation \beta with c = 3N crossings encoding N Toffoli gates, let \mathcal{R}(L) be its Skein resolution tree, with 3^c leaves, and let P_L(q) be the degree-0 observable to which the Markov trace collapses \mathcal{R}(L). A computational horizon for L is a jet horizon \mathcal{H}_c \subset \mathcal{R}(L) with the following three properties.

  1. Degree-0 opacity. The evaluation P_L(q_0), which gives the yes/no answer of the decision problem, cannot be extracted from any polynomial-depth subtree of \mathcal{R}(L).
  2. Degree \geq 1 leakage. Each individual resolution path, as degree-1 linear transport data, admits verification in O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) Planck steps by checking crossing consistencies.
  3. Bandwidth saturation. With information bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q) per Planck time, extracting the degree-0 answer by exploring all 3^c paths demands
  t  \geq  \frac{c \cdot \log 3}{\mathfrak{B}(q)} \cdot  3^{c - c_0}

Planck steps whenever interference fails to bound the effective tree size polynomially.

Jet horizon Computational horizon

prop:p-bandwidth-bound:

  t(c) \leq \mathfrak{B}(q)^{-1} \mathrm{poly}(c)

Planck steps, where \mathfrak{B}(q) = q\eta_q / (q-1)^2 is the information bandwidth per Planck time.
prf:p-bandwidth-bound:
Proof Proof of p bandwidth bound. Sketch. For the forward direction, one uses the standard simulation. If a polynomial-time Turing machine decides the problem, one encodes it as a braid with c = O(\mathrm{poly}(N)) crossings. The transfer matrix product (transfer matrix) computes P_L(q) using O(c) matrix multiplications. Each multiplication costs O(1) Planck steps.

For the converse, one observes that extracting P_L(q_0) requires resolving the value of a degree \leq c^2 - 1 polynomial at a specific point. Suppose the factored form P_L(q) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i(q) has O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) factors. Then one computes each factor in O(1) steps from the local transfer matrix, making the total cost polynomial. If the factored form requires \omega(\mathrm{poly}(c)) factors, the Skein polynomial fails to compress. The information content of the computation exceeds the polynomial bandwidth budget.
rem:p-bandwidth-interpretation:

Cancellation among the 3^c Skein histories allows the Markov trace to compress the tree to O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) surviving terms. In each Planck step, the q-connection \nabla_q processes n_R(q) = 1/\hbar_q iterations. Each iteration generates \eta_q q-bits of entropy. After t Planck steps, the total information budget is:

  I(t) = t \mathfrak{B}(q) = t \frac{q\eta_q}{(q-1)^2} \quad q\text{-bits.}

Polynomial-bandwidth extraction succeeds when I(\mathrm{poly}(c)) suffices to determine P_L(q_0). Although the full resolution tree carries c \log_2 3 q-bits of raw information, destructive interference limits the effective content to O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) q-bits, fitting within the polynomial budget.

Three regimes.

Regime Condition Interpretation

In the sub-horizon regime, the Markov trace funnels the 3^c paths through the degree-0 bottleneck in polynomial time. The computation avoids any computational horizon; the answer remains accessible from a polynomial-depth subtree.

In the super-horizon regime, the resolution tree retains irreducible exponential weight. The uncancelled paths carry independent information requiring full aggregation. Because the bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q) per Planck step is finite, this demands exponentially many steps. A computational horizon strictly separates the answer from the observer.
def:polynomial-observable-subcategory:

prop:block-rigidity:
Proposition Derivations and automorphisms respect the blocks. Let A be an associative algebra over a commutative ring R, and let z \in A be a central idempotent: z^2 = z and za = az for every a \in A.

  1. Every derivation D of A satisfies D(z) = 0, and hence D(za) = z\,D(a) for every a. So D maps the block zA into itself.
  2. Every algebra automorphism of A sends central idempotents to central idempotents.
  3. Every inner automorphism x \mapsto u x u^{-1} fixes every central element. Hence an automorphism that moves a central element is not inner.

For a split semisimple Hecke algebra H_n(K, q), the central primitive idempotents are the units of the Wedderburn blocks. So no derivation mixes blocks, and an automorphism can be visibly outer at the level of the centre only by permuting blocks. The Goldman–Iwahori involution \theta(\sigma_i) = -\sigma_i^{-1} is of this kind: it exchanges the two one-dimensional characters \sigma_i \mapsto q and \sigma_i \mapsto -q^{-1}.
prf:block-rigidity:
Proof Proof that derivations and automorphisms respect the blocks. Apply the Leibniz rule to z = z^2: D(z) = D(z)z + zD(z) = 2zD(z), using that z commutes with D(z). Multiplying on the left by z gives zD(z) = 2z^2D(z) = 2zD(z), so zD(z) = 0, and then D(z) = 2zD(z) = 0. For any a, D(za) = D(z)a + zD(a) = zD(a).

If \varphi is an automorphism, then \varphi(z)^2 = \varphi(z^2) = \varphi(z), and every element of A is \varphi(b) for some b, with \varphi(z)\varphi(b) = \varphi(zb) = \varphi(bz) = \varphi(b)\varphi(z).

If z is central and u is a unit, then uzu^{-1} = zuu^{-1} = z. An automorphism of the form x \mapsto uxu^{-1} therefore fixes z, so one that moves z is not of that form. \square
prop:bounded-width-trace-cost:
Proposition A fixed-width trace costs linear time, not 3^c. Let K be a commutative semiring and let M_1, \dots, M_c be d \times d matrices over K. Applying the word to each standard basis vector, right to left, and summing the diagonal entries computes \mathrm{tr}(M_1 \cdots M_c) with d \cdot c \cdot d^2 multiplications in K. For fixed d this count is at most d^3 c, so it is not super-polynomial in c.

Consequently a braid word on a fixed number n of strands, acting through a representation of fixed dimension (the regular representation of H_n has dimension n!), has a Markov trace computable with O(c) ring operations, with no use of the 3^c leaves of the skein resolution tree. Every family of braids with bounded strand number therefore has an empty computational horizon, and any family with a non-empty computational horizon must have unboundedly many strands. The count is in ring operations; the growth of coefficients in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], which is polynomial in c, is not counted here.
prf:bounded-width-trace-cost: Proof Proof that a fixed-width trace costs linear time. By induction on the word, applying M_1, \dots, M_c to a vector v one at a time returns (M_1 \cdots M_c)v and uses c matrix–vector products of d^2 multiplications each. Applied to the standard basis vector e_i, the i-th entry of the result is the diagonal entry (M_1 \cdots M_c)_{ii}, so summing over the d basis vectors gives the trace with d \cdot c \cdot d^2 multiplications. Since d \cdot c \cdot d^2 = d^3 \cdot c^1, the polynomial d^3 c is never exceeded. \square
prop:jvw-tractable-orders: Proposition Orders of the Jones-tractable points. Jaeger, Vertigan and Welsh show that exact evaluation of the Jones polynomial V_L(t) is \#\mathrm{P}-hard except at the six points t \in \{1, -1, i, -i, e^{2\pi i/3}, e^{-2\pi i/3}\} [jaeger1990]; this is cited, not derived. These six points are primitive roots of unity of orders 1, 2, 4, 4, 3, 3. None of them is a primitive 6th root of unity, and i has order 4, which does not divide 6. So with t = q the orders of the tractable points form the set \{1, 2, 3, 4\}, not \{n : n \mid 6\}. With t = q^{\pm 2} the orders of q form \{1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8\}, which is not \{n : n \mid 6\} either.
prf:jvw-tractable-orders: Proof Proof of the orders of the Jones-tractable points. 1 has order 1 and -1 has order 2. Since i^2 = -1 and i^4 = 1, i is a primitive 4th root of unity, and -i = i^3 is one too because \gcd(3, 4) = 1. The number \omega = e^{2\pi i/3} is a primitive cube root of unity, and so is \omega^{-1}. A primitive root of unity has a unique order, so none of the six points is a primitive 6th root. Finally 4 \nmid 6. \square
thm:geometry-of-incompleteness:
Theorem The geometry of incompleteness: a Turing-complete QOU has a nonempty horizon. Given a QOU whose aether is Turing-complete, the jet horizon \mathcal{H} = V(\mathfrak{h}) is non-empty: there exists a degree-0 datum whose truth is inaccessible. Equivalently, the degree-0 sections vanish on a non-trivial region, \Gamma(\mathcal{H}, A_0) = 0.

A degree-0 datum is an observable answer read off the aether — a decision result, a particle identity, or the truth value of a self-referential sentence. It is inaccessible — behind the horizon — when it fails either route to access:

  • formally, it is unprovable (Gödel incompleteness, forced in any aether expressive enough to encode arithmetic — every q \neq 1 aether, whose q-Toffoli gates are universal); or

These are two witnesses of one phenomenon — the vanishing of degree-0 sections. Gödel supplies a formally-inaccessible degree-0 datum; the resolution-tree information bound supplies a physically-intractable one. Either establishes a non-empty horizon; the QOU exhibits both, so the horizon is doubly confirmed. In the framework's reading, this common cause is exactly what a black-hole event horizon is: the region across which degree-0 truth cannot pass while degree-\geq 1 data (witnesses, Hawking radiation) leaks. The event horizon is the geometry of incompleteness.

Scope. This is an existence statement about the aether's section structure: a Turing-complete QOU hosts an inaccessible degree-0 region via Gödel's incompleteness theorem and via the bandwidth bound on naive 3^{3n}-leaf skein-tree inspection. Only the identification of this joint degree-0 vanishing with a physical horizon is an interpretive reading of the model.

prop:q-exponential-taylor:
Proposition Taylor series of \exp_q (archimedean). Let R be a commutative ring of characteristic zero in which all Jackson factorials [n]_q! = \prod_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1 - q^k}{1 - q} are invertible. Over R, the convergent power series

  \exp_q(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} \frac{x^n}{[n]_q!}

represents the abstract grouplike \exp_q \in G(\mathcal{H}_q).

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs—real-valued physical observables, bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at q_0. Categorical identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is strictly specialised here.
prf:q-exponential-taylor:
Proof Proof of q exponential taylor. The categorical defining equation D_q\, \exp_q = \exp_q, joined with the boundary condition \exp_q(0) = 1, determines a unique formal power series \exp_q(x) = \sum_{n\ge 0} a_n x^n in R[\![x]\!]. The Jackson derivative acts on monomials via D_q(x^n) = [n]_q\, x^{n-1}. One substitutes this into the equation:

  D_q\,\sum_n a_n x^n
  \;=\; \sum_{n \ge 0} a_n [n]_q x^{n-1}
  \;=\; \sum_{m \ge 0} a_{m+1} [m+1]_q x^m.

Equating this to \sum_m a_m x^m forces the recursion a_{m+1} = a_m / [m+1]_q. With a_0 = 1, one obtains:

  a_n \;=\; \prod_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{[k]_q} \;=\; \frac{1}{[n]_q!}.

This verifies the claimed coefficient. Convergence on a neighbourhood of 0 holds because [n]_q! \to \infty faster than geometrically when |q| < 1 or |q| > 1. When |q| = 1, write q = e^{2\pi i\theta}; for irrational \theta convergence holds by Diophantine estimates on \theta. This series provides the archimedean realisation of the universal grouplike. prf:q-gaussian-solves-q-heat:
Proof Proof of q gaussian solves q heat. One decomposes \Delta_q into its three components:

  \Delta_q \;=\; q^{-2} \Delta
  + q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})\,\mathfrak{C}
  + (1 - q^{-1})^2\,\Delta_\xi.

The operator \mathfrak{C} is the Coriolis cross-coupling and \Delta_\xi is the pure Reeb-spin Laplacian. Both \mathfrak{C} and \Delta_\xi contain at least one factor of \mathcal{L}_\xi or \iota_\xi.

The Gaussian G_q depends only on the base coordinates x \in M, not on the Reeb-fibre direction. Therefore,

  \mathcal{L}_\xi G_q = 0,
  \qquad
  \iota_\xi G_q = 0.

Both the Coriolis and spin contributions vanish on G_q:

  -\Delta_q G_q \;=\; -q^{-2} \Delta G_q \;=\; q^{-2} \nabla^2 G_q.

Here \nabla^2 = \sum \partial_i^2 is the non-positive analyst's Laplacian and \Delta = -\nabla^2 is the non-negative Hodge Laplacian. Direct differentiation yields

  \partial_t G_q \;=\; G_q \left(
    -\frac{n}{2t} + \frac{q^2 |x|^2}{4t^2}
  \right),
  \quad
  \nabla^2 G_q \;=\; G_q \left(
    -\frac{n q^2}{2 t} + \frac{q^4 |x|^2}{4 t^2}
  \right).

Multiplying the second equation by q^{-2} yields the first. Hence \partial_t G_q = -\Delta_q G_q. The initial-data condition G_q(t,\cdot) \to \delta_0 as t \downarrow 0 follows from standard properties of the Gaussian heat kernel. \square

Existence at arbitrary q > 0. The formula for G_q defines a classical Gaussian with variance \sigma^2 = t/q^2. It is convergent and strictly positive for every q > 0 and t > 0. At the physical aether value q_0 \approx 1.11 (local aether q), the q-Gaussian

  G_{q_0}(t, x) \;=\; \bigl(4\pi t / q_0^2\bigr)^{-n/2}

is a strict density with variance \sigma^2 \approx 0.81\,t. This is narrower than the classical Gaussian by a factor of q_0^{-2} \approx 0.81. No convergence obstruction appears in the archimedean realisation of the q-heat kernel at q_0 > 1.

prop:q-heat-kernel-peter-weyl:
Proposition Peter--Weyl decomposition of the q-heat kernel (archimedean). Applying the categorical Fourier transform to the q-heat equation diagonalises the q-Laplacian on each Peter--Weyl isotypic component of \mathbf{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)), yielding an explicit spectral formula for the q-heat kernel in two parts.

  1. Spectral decomposition. A solution u \colon \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \times \mathcal{S} \to \mathbb{C} to \partial_t u = -\Delta_q u with initial datum u_0 decomposes as
  u(t, x) = \sum_{\lambda \in \widehat{H_n(q)}} d_\lambda(q) \cdot e^{-\mu_\lambda(q)\,t} \cdot \pi_\lambda(u_0)(x).

The sum ranges over irreducible Wedderburn blocks of the Hecke algebra H_n(q), equivalently indexed by partitions \lambda \vdash n. The dimension d_\lambda(q) is the Steinberg q-hook dimension, \pi_\lambda projects onto the V_\lambda-isotypic component, and \mu_\lambda(q) denotes the q-Laplacian eigenvalue.

  1. Explicit content-Casimir formula. Given a partition \lambda \vdash n with cell contents c(\square) = j - i, the Reeb-spin eigenvalue on V_\lambda is
  \mu_\lambda(q) = \sum_{\square \in \lambda}  [c(\square)]_q \, [c(\square) + 1]_q,

where [k]_q = (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1}) is the symmetric quantum integer. It is the eigenvalue on V_\lambda of the Reeb-holonomy Laplacian

  \Delta_\xi^{(q)} = (q - q^{-1})^{-2} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \bigl( q\,H_k + q^{-1} H_k^{-1} - (q + q^{-1}) \bigr), \qquad H_k = (\Delta^2_{k-1})^{-1}\Delta^2_k,

where \Delta^2_k is the full twist of the first k+1 strands. Each H_k is the k-th Jucys--Murphy element of H_n(q), and \Delta_\xi^{(q)} is central. Writing q = e^{h}, each summand is a symmetric second difference of step h, and as h \to 0 the operator tends to \sum_k X_k(X_k+1), where X_k are the classical Jucys--Murphy elements. So \Delta_\xi^{(q)} is the finite-step form of the Reeb Laplacian \mathcal{L}_\xi^*\mathcal{L}_\xi, with a half-integer shift. The Reeb part of \Delta_q enters with weight 1, not \hbar_q^2: on a mode with no horizontal derivative, d_q and \delta_q reduce to d and \delta, because q^{-1} + \hbar_q = 1. The classical-core and cross-coupling terms of rem:q-laplacian-expansion act on such modes as well, and the three coefficients sum to (q^{-1} + \hbar_q)^2 = 1. The spatial part contributes a separate eigenvalue q^{-2}|\mathbf{k}|^2, dependent on the spatial wavenumber \mathbf{k}.

Scope note. The eigenvalue formula uses symmetric q-integers and unit Reeb weight (no \hbar_q^2 prefactor); both choices are derived below rather than fitted. What is proved: the operator is central. Its Jucys--Murphy elements are relative full twists. Its eigenvalue on a Jucys--Murphy weight vector is (q-q^{-1})^2\sum[c][c+1]. The weight vectors exist for generic q by the seminormal form. What is not proved: that \Delta^2_k is the holonomy of the Reeb rotation loop of the cluster of the first k+1 points. That identification is Bridge A (the n-body base with \xi the Euler field, plus Drinfeld--Kohno). The weight-1 argument for the Reeb part is written out below; unlike the statements listed as proved, it has not been independently checked. Proof. Schur's lemma on the irreducible Wedderburn block forces any central element to act by a scalar. For \Delta_\xi^{(q)} that scalar is computed on a Jucys--Murphy weight vector. There H_k = L_k acts by q^{2c_k}, and each summand becomes (q^{c} - q^{-c})(q^{c+1} - q^{-c-1}) = (q - q^{-1})^2[c][c+1]. Summing over k gives \mu_\lambda(q). The value [c][c+1] is unchanged under c \mapsto -c-1, so each cell contributes the U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) Casimir value at spin c or -c-1, whichever is non-negative.

The Reeb part carries no \hbar_q^2. Let f be a mode with df = (\xi f)\,\varTheta. Then d_q f = q^{-1}(\xi f)\varTheta + \hbar_q(\xi f)\varTheta = df.
